characters.name: Beavis
characters.description: Beavis is (even) dumber than Butt-Head, and more than a little crazy. He has an alter ego called "The Great Cornholio" that emerges when he has too much sugar or caffeine. Adaptational Intelligence:Do Americadepicts him as aGenius Ditzwho's slightly smarter than Butt-Head. Affably Evil: Well...evilmaybe a bit of a stretch, but he's genuinely outgoing with people whenever he's not creating chaos with Butt-Head, being sincerely pleasant to the old woman he sits next to and meets repeatedly in "Do America". Ambiguous Innocence: On the one hand, Beavis' head is always in the gutter; he has an appetite for destruction and a disturbing obsession with fire. However, he can also be polite when left to his own devices, is capable of enjoying more childish pursuits, and has the impression that a relationship can involve more than just sex, implying he may just be a dumb kid who doesn't know any better. "It's a Miserable Life" shows that without Butt-Head, Beavis could have grown up to become a decent, if still incredibly dim, person, showing his worst aspects are due to Butt-Head's influence, bullying, and pressure. That said, when Butt-Headdoesbecome a nicer person in "Nice Butt-Head", Beavis becomes furious and eventually gives Butt-Head aNo-Holds-Barred Beatdownto try and restore him to his previous self. Apologetic Attacker: One thing that sets him apart from Butt-Head is that he can occasionally say sorry for some of his actions and show something like sincere remorse.

characters.name: Butt-Head
characters.description: The series's other protagonist, Butt-Head isslightlymore intelligent than Beavis (for whatever that's worth) and usually comes up with the duo'sZany Schemesto meet girls or make money. Although he's generally calmer and more mentally stable than his partner, he's also more prone to violence. Aw, Look! They Really Do Love Each Other:While he and Beavis have their moments of spats, they are relatively best buddies through and through. When he's on the verge of death,he remarks that a life spent doing nothing but bumming around with Beavis was "cool".In the reboot, Butt-Head seriously injures Beavis by kicking him in the nads too many times, and the thought of his best friend dying puts him in a depression. While he and Beavis have their moments of spats, they are relatively best buddies through and through. When he's on the verge of death,he remarks that a life spent doing nothing but bumming around with Beavis was "cool". In the reboot, Butt-Head seriously injures Beavis by kicking him in the nads too many times, and the thought of his best friend dying puts him in a depression. Bad Bedroom, Bad Life: As seen in "Scientific Stuff", Butt-Head's room is a chaotic mess, with dirt, random objects, and empty cans strewn across the floor. The walls are grimy, and the bed is unmade. He never seems to sleep there, although he likely wouldn't mind the mess if he ever did.

characters.name: Smart Beavis and Smart Butt-Head
characters.description: Alternate Self: The smartest versions of Beavis and Butt-Head, relatively speaking. They're highly intelligent on a cosmic scale but still somewhat lacking in common sense and competency similar to their main counterparts. Alternate Universe Reed Richards Is Awesome: They hail from a highly advanced universe that has technology "you could only dream of" including the ability to access porn in any scenario you could imagine. Batman Can Breathe in Space: They can breathe and talk on the moon and in outer space. Bigger Is Better in Bed: Smart Beavis claims to have a "gigantic schlong" and hopes this isn't a deal-breaker with Serena. Bizarre Alien Biology: Implied in "Abduction." Smart Beavis needs to be reminded how many anuses a human has, and their probing device has a dial that goes up to two.

characters.name: Old Beavis
characters.description: Absurdly Dedicated Worker:As Old Butt-Head thinks that being unemployed is his job, Old Beavis is usually the breadwinner between the two. Usually, he donates sperm "kind of everywhere" and blood for extra money, although he has donated so much that it's now considered too watery.In "Home Aide" because he's maxed out his unemployment benefits, he gets the titular job. Compared to his younger self, he actually does what to do the job he's told to, but Old Butt-Head takes advantage of it to treat him like a servant. As Old Butt-Head thinks that being unemployed is his job, Old Beavis is usually the breadwinner between the two. Usually, he donates sperm "kind of everywhere" and blood for extra money, although he has donated so much that it's now considered too watery. In "Home Aide" because he's maxed out his unemployment benefits, he gets the titular job. Compared to his younger self, he actually does what to do the job he's told to, but Old Butt-Head takes advantage of it to treat him like a servant. The Alcoholic: Now that he's legally old enough, his preferred drink is beer, and his favorite brand is Saint Ides. Ascended Extra: Alongside Old Butt-Head, he had one short scene inBeavis and Butt-Head Do the Universe. In the 2022 revival series, he's become a semi-regular with Old Butt-Head and receives plenty of focus episodes.

characters.name: Old Butt-Head
characters.description: The Alcoholic: Like Old Beavis, Old Butt-Head takesmassiveadvantage of the fact that he's now of legal drinking age. He's often seen guzzling beer, and spends as much money as he can on it. Unlike Beavis, he'll even prioritize getting more beer over groceries. Ascended Extra: He only had one short scene with Old Beavis inBeavis and Butt-Head Do the Universe. In the 2022 revival series which takes place after the second movie, Old Butt-head is turned into a series semi-regular alongside Old Beavis, with the two of them getting more focus. Big Guy, Little Guy: He towers over Old Beavis, who doesn't seem to have grown at all since his teen years. Costume Evolution: Like Old Beavis, Old Butt-Head has long ditched his black AC-DC shirt for a white one with a brown short-sleeved jacket, and grey shorts instead of red. Disproportionate Retribution: He cripples Old Beavis with his mobility scooter simply because the latter wanted to buy Count Chocula instead of beer at the supermarket.

characters.name: Empress Beavis and Emperor Butt-Head
characters.description: Chuck Cunningham Syndrome: They aren't mentioned in the revival TV show with Smart Beavis and Butthead taking orders from the Supreme Leaders who are composed of smart version of otherBeavis and Butt-Headcharacters. No Historical Figures Were Harmed: Designed to resemble Queen Victoria and Prince Albert. Sexless Marriage: Implied, as Smart Beavis is honored as the first among them to score. Vocal Dissonance: Empress Beavis' voice is just prime Beavis' voice pitch shifted.

characters.name: Stewart Stevenson
characters.description: A hapless nerd who hangs out with Beavis and Butt-Head — not because they like him, but because he'll let them get away with almost anything. All for Nothing: In the alternate universe of the 2022 revival where Beavis and Butt-Head never time traveled, an adult Stewart returns to Highland to become a kidney donor to Beavis, only for Beavis to insult him cruelly many times, show no appreciation for Stewart's effort, anddestroy Stewart's transplanted kidney inside his body before the day is even over. Alliterative Name: His last and first name begins with a "St" sound. Big Fun: He might be chubby, but he’s really friendly guy who wants to have fun. It becomes more noticeable in his adulthood, where he’s more boisterous and attached to Beavis and Butt-Head. He even came up with the idea to start drinking with the duo. Butt-Monkey: Beavis and Butt-Head constantly give him grief, whether it be teasing him, getting him in trouble with authorities, taking advantage of him, or getting him and his family on the wrong side of a violent thug. And all he wants to do is hang out with them.

characters.name: Daria Morgendorffer
characters.description: Daria is one of Beavis and Butt-Head's classmates. Intelligent but disaffected, she's amused by the duo's antics, and often makes sarcastic remarks that go right over their heads. Actually Pretty Funny:A moment in the episode "The Trial"has her cracking up when Butt-Head said "I rest on your face" in court. Adaptational Angst Upgrade: In the Marvel comics, not only does Daria have to read fan mail from readers in the "Dear Diarrhea" section but she had the added plight of having to listen to shippers talk about how Daria secretly desires Beavis and Butt-Head or should hook up with them, which does a number on her mentally. So sheknewthere were Beavis/Daria and Butt-head/Daria shippers out there and had no choice but to listen to them talk about how they wanted her with one of the two.Daria:ALL RIGHT! That's IT! For the record… I would rather sunbathe naked on Mercury without suntan lotion than go out with either Beavis or Butt-Head. Adaptational Nice Girl: A minor example. In the Marvel tie-in comics, herrelationship with the two is worse than in the show in some ways, with her even getting the two left behind on an Amish farm once and the two being more insulting to her. However, in the show, she never once expressed any hope for the two to learn or better themselves, nor does she allow the boys any entry into her personal life. But in the comics, she allows the duo to stay at her home for holiday events like Halloween and Christmas. And for the Christmas issue, she even relents and tells the duo that the meaning of Christmas is peace on earth and goodwill to all men, a meaning that's lost on Beavis and Butt-Head but for Daria, it was probably the kindest gesture Daria had given them in a non-TV medium and showed she did want to help them better themselves on some level. Adaptation Relationship Overhaul:In the Marvel tie-in comics, Beavis and Butt-Head are somewhat nastier to her than they were in the show, often making rude remarks about her appearance and notably

characters.name: Cassandra
characters.description: Another of B&B's classmates, Cassandra is a hippie-ish aspiring artist of possible Asian descent. She doesn't get much screen time, but the series hints that she has some disturbingHidden Depths. Ambiguously Bi: A big fan of notoriously lesbian singerk.d. lang, though she also expresses a fondness for older men in other episodes. It's unclear if she herself really has same sex attractions or she simply loves k.d. lang's music and is open minded enough that she doesn't care about the singer's sexuality. Chuck Cunningham Syndrome: She is absent from the 2022 revival, since she would've long graduated from Highland High at that point, and while her character design was reused in the 2011 revival (albeit without glasses), she never spoke and it was never confirmed to be her. Granola Girl: Like Van Driessen, she's a nature-loving hippie. Hot for Teacher: Her story about how a teenage girl and her English teacher drown together implies she might be attracted to Mr. Van Driessen

characters.name: Dean Zunker
characters.description: Ambiguously Gay: He repeatedly asks Beavis and Butt-Head why he never sees them take showers in “Wet Behind the Rears,” which makes them visibly uncomfortable. Big Eater: He is rather chubby and sometimes shown eating in class. Chuck Cunningham Syndrome: He only appeared in the original series and the 2011 revival, being completely absent from the 2022 revival. Justified, since Dean would be all grown up and have long graduated from Highland High by 2022. Depending on the Writer: Dean could either be friendly to the duo much like Stewart or be apathetic towards them depending on the episode. Living Prop: He doesn't have much prominence or personality besides being one of Beavis and Butt-Head's classmates, and his speaking appearances are very sporadic.

characters.name: Earl
characters.description: One of the students of Highland High. He is a thug who brandishes a pistol. Adaptation Relationship Overhaul: In the Marvel Comics series, he and Todd are shown to be close friends and frequently hang out in the same social circles. In the show, Earl never once talked to Todd. Ascended Extra: He plays a much bigger role in the Marvel Comics series and is shown to be friends with Todd. Chuck Cunningham Syndrome: He is absent from the 2011 revival, which is notable since most of the other students appeared, and doesn't appear in the 2022 revival due to having long graduated from Highland High at that point. A Day in the Limelight: A central character inIncognitoas he threatened to harm the boys.

characters.name: Martin
characters.description: One of the students of Highland High. Originally a gifted student, until, when performing a dangerous experiment on his brain, Beavis tripped on the wire, causing his experiment to malfunction and his intelligence to dramatically decrease, as well as him being forced to move down to B&B's class for the rest of the show. Chuck Cunningham Syndrome: He doesn't appear in the 2022 revival, due to having long graduated from Highland High at that point. Demoted to Extra: After his first appearance, he was relegated to voiceless cameos as another one of Beavis and Butt-Head's classmates, only having one more speaking role in theVirtual Stupidityvideo game. Ditzy Genius: Apparently, he didn't take proper safety precautions for his own brain-enhancing experiment, sinceanyonecould've easily tripped over the wire. Fat Bastard: He is overweight and was condescending as aTeen Genius. When his brain experiment went haywire, he became aFat Idiot.

characters.name: Cody
characters.description: One of the students of Highland High in the 2022 revival, who regularly talks down to the duo. Contrasting Replacement Character: Cody seems to take Stewart's place as the chubby classmate of the duo's who is shown interacting with them the most. However, unlike Stewart, Codyloathesthe boys, and is overall more mature, assertive, stoic and less friendly in general. A Day in the Limelight: He gets a spotlight episode in the Season 10 finale "Sleepover". Deadpan Snarker: Has a razor sharp wit that could almost rival Daria's, with the stoicism to go with it. Didn't Think This Through: He invites the duo over in "Sleepover" just because he wanted to make them watch him play video games, for apparently no other reason than to be a dick. What he didn't foresee was how his parents would take a shine to the two, the two humiliating him, them being allowed to spend the night, and the duo finally walking off with his video game console.

characters.name: Glennis
characters.description: A blue-haired student in the 2022 revival who develops a crush on Beavis, who, of course, doesn't realize it and thinks she wants to beat him up. Break the Cutie: Whenit seems like Beavis is about to return his feelings for her in front of the class,he instead exclaims that he loves fire, leaving her heartbroken and resorting to arson in an attempt to impress him. The Bus Came Back: Originally aOne-Shot Characterfor "Weird Girl", since she was arrested for arson, but made a silent cameo during B&B's fantasy in "Nacho Shake" as one of the girls hugging Beavis. Eating Lunch Alone: At the start of the episode, she is eating a sandwich by herself in the cafeteria. Friendless Background: She eats lunch alone, and her classmates don't seem to like her, as Cody calls her "the weird girl in Van Driessen's class".

characters.name: Audrey
characters.description: A Christian classmate of Beavis and Butt-Head's in the 2022 revival. She is part of an abstinence group and Highland's outreach program. Accidental Misnaming: She constantly gets the duo's names wrong, calling Beavis "Bobby" and "Baxter", and Butt-Head "Broderick". Church Lady: Of the Positive variety, but with a twist. She's a Christian girl who genuinely tries to be helpful. However, she can still get worn down by the antics of Beavis and Butthead to the point of growing fed up with them, so she's just pious enough to be genuine and charitable without the gossipy, entitled traits of the more Negative Church Lady... but still human enough to grow tired of the duo's antics. Hair of Gold, Heart of Gold: Audrey has blonde hair and is a kindhearted individual. Nice Girl: Audrey is very caring, and is one of the very few female characters to be genuinely cordial towards the duo. She is well aware that they are obsessed with sex, but still tries to help them out by inviting them to her abstinence group to try to get them to focus on their studies. She was also concerned about Beavis when he was depressed over his "nut" allergy.

characters.name: David Van Driessen
characters.description: Abusive Parents:This Book Suckscontains the lyrics to several of his songs. "Chopping Wood With My Father" describes how Van Driessen's father was astereotypical man's manwho considered him a weakling "hippy freak" despite Van Driessen's attempts to get him to love him. Van Driessen's brother Tom was a strong, athletic soldier who their fatherfavored, and whoviolently punched Van Driessenwhen Tom was killed in Qatar. The only time Van Driessen and his father were close was when they were chopping wood, and now he's dying from Alzheimer's. It's implied that Van Driessen won't be sad to see him go. Aesop Amnesia: He's repeatedly learned that Beavis and Butt-Head are crude, destructive morons (particularly notable in the episode where they "clean" his house), yet continues to rather naively support and encourage them. Though it's justified as Van Driessen has an optimism very uncharacteristic of the Highland High staff. Animals Hate Him: Ironically for a hippie. His hippyish activities (usually playing awful country music) tend to result in him getting attacked by wild animals in the vicinity. To wit, he's been mauled by a bear (twice), ravaged by a mountain lion, and attacked by an eagle while hang-gliding. Thankfully, this is averted when he's dealing with domesticated animals, like the cat he adopted in "A.I." Berserk Button: He's very protective of his eight-tracks; Beavis and Butt-Head destroying his entire collection marked the one time in the series he angrily expressed an interest in killing them (though he also immediately got buried underneath said collection). The rest of the time, however, he won't stand for them or any of his students being physically harmed by someone. Beware the Nice Ones: Surprisingly, Van Driessen is very protective of Beavis and Butt-Head, despite how poorly they treat him. In "Manners Suck", he physically attacks Mr. Manners after Beavis falsely implies that Mr. Manners molested him.Van Driessen:(slapping Mr. Manners)You wanna touch

characters.name: Coach Buzzcut
characters.description: A macho, ill-tempered veteran, Mr. Buzzcut is Beavis and Butt-Head's gym teacher. He tries to keep them under control through constant verbal — and often physical — abuse. Although he takes the opposite approach from Van Driessen, the dumbass duo show him only a margin of respect on account that he will kick their asses if they piss him off. Alliterative Name: Although his first name is never used in the series and only appears in the books and comics. Ambiguously Gay: He has never displayed interest in women,he seemed to really enjoy Butt-Headkicking him in the Jimmy, he has the boys as a gay couple inA Baby Makes, Uhh, Three, and in "Wet Behind The Rears" not only did he try to get them naked in public, but he also gotrather offended when Butt-Head insinuated that he likes watching dudes take a shower. Berserk Button:Never punch him, even if you are about as strong asMr Burns.Ever!Coach Buzzcut:(face getting red with rage)You just made a fatal mistake, Mr. Candy-Ass!I hope you know something about hand-to-hand combat!Don't you dare tell him that you don't know anything about the Founding Fathers of America.Don't hit his students. Only he can do that. Never punch him, even if you are about as strong asMr Burns.Ever!Coach Buzzcut:(face getting red with rage)You just made a fatal mistake, Mr. Candy-Ass!I hope you know something about hand-to-hand combat!

characters.name: PrincipalMcVicker
characters.description: A nervous, high-strung bureaucrat who lives in terror of B&B and occasionally tries to get rid of them. Of course, he always fails. The Alcoholic: Has been driven to drinking and pill popping by the duo's antics. Anti-Villain: He's the closest thing Beavis and Butt-Head have to anArch-Enemybut is legitimately trying to run an educational institute for the sake of learning in the face of the pair constantly being disruptive. Arch-Enemy: He's the most recurring antagonist the duo face throughout the series before the revival despite not being an actual "bad guy" and both sides tend to hate each other, withMcVicker's feelings of personal hatred and loathing for two always skyrocketing because of how much stress and terrible times they put him through. Back from the Dead: Although he apparently died of a heart attack at the end of Season 7, he appears in the season 8 episodeDumb Designproving that he wasn't dead after all. And even with the 2011 series being overridden by the 2022 revival, he's still shown at the 1998 trial for Beavis and Butt-head inBeavis and Butt-Head Do the Universe, revealing he did survive the events of "Beavis And Butt-Head Are Dead".

characters.name: Tom Anderson
characters.description: The duo's next-door neighbor and frequent victim. He's smart enough to realize that the boys are a menace, but too old and senile to do anything about it. Notably, he served as the prototype forHank Hill. Accidental Misnaming: He's referred to our heroes as everything from "Buford and Bernardo" to "Butt-Hole and Joe". This continues even decades later, when he addresses the middle-aged Beavis and Butt-Head as "Belvis and Bunhowzen" when they pretend to be veterans to get beer at the Legion. Aesop Amnesia: Keeps rehiring the duo because he keeps forgetting what they look like, despite wrecking his yard every time. He does eventually catch on and stops hiring helpers for his yard work, not that it stops Beavis and Butt-Head from ruining things. Ascended Extra: A mild example, as Anderson had always been a major supporting character in the original series. However, in the 2022 revival, he's given just a little more spotlight and even gets his own shorts describing his (mis)adventures during wartime. And ultimately, given how many previous important supporting characters likeMcVicker, Buzzcut, Stewart, the Burger World manager, Todd, and Daria are either gone, replaced, orDemoted to Extra, Tom Anderson's prominence in the 2022 series has gone up as a side effect, with Anderson now possibly being the third most important character in the show after the titular duo. Badass on Paper: He's a decorated war veteran without any apparent dishonorable discharge and he has enough medals on his wall in his war story shorts to show that he has the official accolades. But how much of a truly badass warrior he was in the past or is in the present day is now legitimately called into question due to many of his wartime story portrayals where he's shown not engaging in any fighting but placesSkewed Prioritieson other things. It also becomes hard to gauge how much of a genuine "badass" he is in the present day because in "Streamroller" when he punched his neighbor out, it was a sucker pu

characters.name: Mr. And Mrs. Stevenson
characters.description: Stewart's less-than-ideal parents. Abusive Parents: A non-physical example, considering he's never shown beating Stewart, but Mr. Stevenson has demonstrated that when confronted with an issue (such as the uncovering of his porno stack), he will essentially try to pin all the blame on Stewart. Not to mention how he was pretty willing to have Stewart get his ass kicked by Harry Sachz to save himself. Mrs. Stevenson doesn't even try to protect her son from Sachz either. Asshole Victim: Despite technically being an innocent victim whom the duo accidentally sic Harry Sachz on, Mr. Stevenson is still shown trying to deflect all the blame on his own son so Stewart can suffer punishment instead of him. As a result, one doesn't have to feeltoobad that hegets assaultedby an enraged Harry Sachz in a case of mistaken identity brought upon by the pair's prank calls. Ass Shove: Mr. Stevenson fell victim to this when Harry Sachz attacked him under the impression that he was the one behind the repeated prank-calls that Sachz had to deal with. The Bus Came Back:Despite being absent in the 2022 revival, an alternate universe alien version of Mrs. Stevenson appears in "Abduction".

characters.name: Maxi-Mart Clerk
characters.description: The clerk at the Maxi-Mart convenience store the duo frequently visit. He is often annoyed with their antics at his store. Apathetic Clerk: He isalways seen unhappy on the job, and expresses dread every time the duo visit his store. Chuck Cunningham Syndrome: He only appeared in the original series run, and is absent from both the 2011 and 2022 revivals (at least two more kempt clerks have been shown taking his place in the latter) Early-Installment Weirdness: The episode "Pool Toys" had him work at a hardware store, while the rest of his appearances have him work exclusively at the Maxi-Mart. Hair-Trigger Temper: It doesn't take much for the duo to piss him off and make him try to kick them out of the Maxi-Mart.

characters.name: Lolita and Tanqueray
characters.description: Two trailer trash girls who are recurring objects of lust for Beavis and Butt-Head. Affectionate Nickname: Tanqueray calls Beavis "sugar britches". Catchphrase: "I'm Lolita, and this here's Tanqueray", for whenever they come across the boys. Catholic School Girls Rule: They are implied to be from a Catholic family in "Tornado" where several statues of the Virgin Mary fly out of their trailer. Chuck Cunningham Syndrome: They appeared in three episodes between 1993 and 1994 and have never appeared again.

characters.name: Hamid
characters.description: A character created for the 2011revival, Hamid appears to be an immigrant from the Middle East. He's yet another adult victim of Beavis and Butt-Head—he's lost two jobs due to their antics. Butt-Monkey: Is constantly on the receiving end of the boys' antics; they have cost him two jobs. Chuck Cunningham Syndrome: Only appeared in 2 episodes and hasn't been seen again since. Funny Foreigner: Appears to be from somewhere in the Middle East. Honest John's Dealership: Hamid himself isn't particularly unscrupulous, but he does end up working for one at one point.

characters.name: Crazy Old Farmer/Janitor
characters.description: A creepy, mysterious old man who appears in only a few episodes—fortunately for Beavis, because this character has killed himtwice. Amazing Technicolor Population: In his more villainous roles, he has pale blue skin. Ambiguously Human: He has a blueUndeathly Pallorand yellow eyes, and in the Halloween episode, he's donesomethingto Butt-Head that causes his skin to turn the same color as his, and has him gleefully join him in murdering Beavis with chainsaws. It's implied that he could be some kind of zombie. Ax-Crazy: Cemented when he kills Beavis. Bald of Evil: He's bald and psycho.

characters.name: Todd Ianuzzi
characters.description: A local thug who is the unwilling recipient of Beavis and Butt-Head's "hero" worship. While he regards the boys with open contempt and frequently beats them up, they admire him too much to leave him alone, and are too stupid to see him as a threat. Adaptational Karma: As supplementary video games usually don't tend to be canon (unless otherwise stated) to a main TV series or its movies, Todd getting completely humiliated by the duo and arrested inVirtual Stupidityis this, being one of the only times he gets punishment in another media format whereas he remained untouched in the show and movies, outside of Beavis having a fantasy where Serena kills him. All Girls Want Bad Boys: Todd is a despicable, cruel, violent, utterly loathsome thug who is aggressive to pretty much everyone he sees. Yet, for some reason, almost every girl in the show has been seen dating him. All Take and No Give: His relationship with the two can best be described as taking whatever he wants from them while giving nothing back, whether it's their food, their money, their possessions, or even temporarily using their home as sanctuary to hide out from the cops or rival gangs. The best the two can hope for is Todd deciding not to beat them up and even then, Todd might still take something from them, like how he stole Cornholio's candy in "Bungholio: Lord of the Harvest" in spite of deciding not to attack a sugar-high Beavis. Anti-Role Model: Beavis and Butt-Head worship him, despite being a ruthless thug.

characters.name: Todd's Gang
characters.description: Todd's cronies, consisting of violent, petty thugs of similar nature. All There in the Manual: Aside from Slade (the portly brunette who is most commonly seen with Todd), who was explicitly addressed by name in his debut, their names have only been revealed through merchandise, such as trading cards, and have never been addressed by them in the show. The tan Earl lookalike is dubbed "Psycho", and the lanky thug with long hair is called JD (although he is referred to as "Pork" in a model sheet) The Bus Came Back: After being absent from the 2022 revival outside of aFantasy SequenceinBeavis and Butt-Head Do the Universe, Slade returns in the Old timeline in the episode "Plumber's Helpers", alongside Leroy (Todd's rival from "Safe House" and theVirtual Stupidityvideo game, who was seen as part of Todd's gang in "Snitchers", his last appearance before then). "Psycho" was also brought back for the aforementioned fantasy after being absent from the 2011 revival, only to disappear again after that. Chuck Cunningham Syndrome: When their leader wasPut on a Busfor the most part in the 2022 revival, they joined him. Before that, JD disappeared after the original series run, and "Psycho" was absent from the 2011 revival (with Leroy and one of his friends taking their place). Flat Character: They're friends of Todd who join him in menacing Beavis and Butt-Head. That's all there is to them.

characters.name: Billy Bob
characters.description: A morbidly obese hillbilly who occasionally gets caught up in the boys' misadventures. Berserk Button: Making off with his scooter isnota good idea... Big Eater: Hinted massively in "Bedpans and Broomsticks", where he is first shown in a doctor's office for artery problems and suffers fromMeat-O-Vision. Chuck Cunningham Syndrome: Only appears in early episodes with the exception of a cameo in "Blackout", although a similar character appears at the end of "Massage" in season 8. Cigar Chomper: He even has one when he's on the treadmill.

characters.name: Harry Sachz
characters.description: An ill-tempered middle-aged man with a history of crime and violence, and a silly-sounding name, which the duo naturally make fun of, and take advantage of in a series of crank calls. Ass Shove: Invokes this on a hapless (but totally deserving) Mr. Stevenson — with aphone— after a combination of too many crank calls from Beavis and Butt-Head and a case of mistaken identity. Ax-Crazy: Given what he ended up doing to Mr. Stevenson, it is safe to say he is severely emotionally unstable, to say the least, and may have issues that go deeper than just Beavis and Butt-head being relentlessly annoying. Back from the Dead: Despite having been gut-shot in "Butt Flambé" and seen dying of his wounds in the hospital, he returns in Season 8. However, since the 2011 revival is no longer canon due toDo the Universe, this may no longer be the case (although a lookalike appears as a veteran in "Stolen Valor"). Bald of Evil: Zig-Zagged. In some episodes, he has some hair growing down from the back, yet the top is empty. Others depict him with some hair on top albeit receding considerably, the “Prank Call” episode has an angle shot of him having full hair on top.

characters.name: Dr. Fisk
characters.description: A local doctor who appears in "Plastic Surgin," "Rabies Scare," "Woodshop," and "Tainted Meat." Seems like a fairly normal character although it's implied the first impression is misleading... Actually Pretty Funny: He describes how in a suspected case of rabies the animal must be captured, euthanized, and the brain dissected for evidence of the disease. Butt-head gets excited and says "Cool!" to which he affirmatively responds "Actually it is kind of cool." Ambiguously Evil: The ending of "Rabies Scare" implies that he intentionally gave Beavis an unnecessarily painful treatment for no real reason. A cutaway to him then shows him diabolically laughing over the fake name Beavis provided at the appointment. The Comically Serious: Other than hisEvil Laughat the end of "Rabies Scare" he never speaks in anything but a standard deadpan tone, no matter how ridiculous or absurd what Beavis and Butt-head are saying in response is. Depending on the Writer: Whether he's portrayed as a normal doctor or an impliedMad Doctorcan vary depending on which episode you see him in.

characters.name: Burger World Manager
characters.description: The manager of Burger World, who's also Beavis and Butt-Head's boss, and a pretty lousy one if he's willing to keep them on board. Benevolent Boss: He's this just by sheer virtue of still keeping Beavis and Butt-Head employed no matter how many times they screw up on the job, get him injured, or ruin the reputation of Burger World beyond salvage. The worst he ever does is scold them, force them to take a lie detector test when he suspects that they have been taking money from the register in "Liar! Liar!", try to attack them at the end of "Work is Death", punish them for going on strike by making them scrape gum from under the tables, and inBeavis and Butt-Head Do Christmas, seemingly slaps Butt-Head off-screen as Beavis dozes off. In any other work of fiction, it would make the Burger World manager aBad Boss... but given everything Butt-Head has done on the job,Butt-Headcomes off as the one who got off lightly with one hit despite ruining the restaurant's reputation multiple times over.That being said, he seems to have finally given up on them in the alternate timeline where the duo didn't time travel, if Beavis being unemployed since 1999 is anything to go by. However, this is never elaborated on. Butt-Monkey: He's often on the bad end of things because the two rarely do their job right, though he ultimately brings it on himself considering he keeps them around despite their gross incompetence. Chuck Cunningham Syndrome: In the 2022 revival, Burger World has a new manager in both timelines. It can be assumed that he either transferred to a new restaurant, was fired for letting Beavis and Butt-Head cause so much trouble for his store or may have simply retired during the long period of time Beavis and Butt-Head went missing/left Burger World. Dude, Where's My Respect?: Even though he is generous enough to keep the two employed and pay them a decent enough salary, they still disrespect him and make no effort to keep his business afloat. Sometimes, they even get on h

characters.name: Burger World Manager ( 2022 revival)
characters.description: The manager of Burger World seen in the 2022 revival. It's unknown how long he's been working there or if he's the immediate replacement of the former manager. Contrasting Replacement Character: He's no less incompetent than the previous manager, but he is nicer to the two and doesn't verbally berate them, even if they deserve it. In "Nacho Shake", he's heavily shaken up by the restaurant being closed down but doesn't take it out on the duo even though they were the most blatantly obvious suspects in causing the 30 day shutdown. Incompetence, Inc.: Probably even more so than his predecessor to where he tolerates the boys. Not even Beavis using the mop to wipe ketchup and mustard on the floors is enough to merit any serious response from the new manager, and he just shoves the mascot costume onto Butt-Head despite Beavis clearly wanting to wear it. He also doesn't do anything about the fracas in his restaurant caused by the duo abusing his "Refuse Service" rule. No Name Given: Just like his predecessor, his name remains a mystery. Pointy-Haired Boss: Doesn't even bat an eye at Beavis mopping greasy, contaminated liquid on the floor right in front of him, and even orders him to keep mopping the floor anyway in spite of it for the sake of "team goals".

characters.name: Mr. Manners
characters.description: An educational speaker who comes to Highland under a different persona, and usually runs afoul of Beavis and Butt-Head. Asshole Victim: Is a pompous salesman, so the audience doesn't feel too bad when Beavis and Butt-Head get him fired and he gets beaten to a pulp by Buzzcut. Bullying a Dragon: Mr. Candydaresto insult Coach Buzzcut and hit him.It. Does. Not. End. Well. Continuity Nod: In "Candy Sale" he says it took him six months to find a job after the events of "Manners Suck". Mistaken for Pedophile: Beavis gets him fired in both of his appearances by claiming that he's touching his "weiner".

characters.name: Shirley Beavis
characters.description: Beavis's mother, whom we never see. Abusive Parents: Beavis and Butt-Head often recall how she would try to abandon Beavis, such as leaving him at an Ikea so she could go to Las Vegas with some bikers; only for the pair to constantly run into one another. The Alcoholic: Beavis mentions how she would often "come down with the liquor flu" and would ignore him as a child. Aw, Look! They Really Do Love Each Other: Even though there are several examples of her being neglectful and outright trying to get rid of Beavis, she was for the most part still part of Beavis’s life (which was mentioned several times to have made accommodations to make sure her son is taken care of when she’s gone and was even there for his birthdays). She was actually devastated to learn that Beavis was killed in space (he wasn’t, but there was no way of knowing that). She apparently loved Beavis enough for him to return that affection, as evidenced by him defending her from insults. Break the Cutie: When she believes that her son hasdied in outer space.

characters.name: Marcie Anderson
characters.description: Tom Anderson's seldom-seen wife. The Bus Came Back: After making a handful of appearances in the show's original run andDo America, she was absent in the 2011 revival andDo the Universe. However, she was mentioned by Tom in "Roof" and "Locked Out" before finally reappearing in the episode "The Good Deed". Flat Character: Since we don't see much of her, she doesn't have much of an established personality besides just being Tom Anderson's wife. Unlike her husband and his inspiration forHank Hill, while Marcie resembles an older Peggy Hill, she isnothinglike her and has no influence on Peggy's character besides her appearance. Happily Married: To Tom. They fondly reminisce their wedding day, and are still shown to be together well intoThe New '20s. Larynx Dissonance: In the original series, Judge voiced her, barely even trying to sound like an elderly woman. Averted in the 2022 revival, where she was voiced by Toks Olagundoye, an actual woman who gave her a more appropriate generic old lady voice.

characters.name: Ellen
characters.description: A local adult and Van Driessen's "lady friend". Beware the Nice Ones: Despite being polite and kind, if you ruin her community garden, she will beat the snot out of you. Granola Girl: She is highly in tune with nature and sells bee honey at the farmer's market. Insistent Terminology: Van Driessen refers to her as his "lady friend", not his girlfriend. Considering how he's later shown having severe trouble with his dating life during the 2020s era in "Swipe Right With David Van Driessen", she may very well just be a platonic female friend of his and nothing more.

characters.name: Keith
characters.description: A newcomer to Highland, who looks like Butt-Head. Doppelgänger: Looks like Butt-Head from a distance, down to wearing a similar outfit, which causes Beavis to at first mistake him for Butt-Head. The Ghost: He constantly mentions his friend Raf, and his girlfriend Marcy, who he wants Beavis to meet. Innocently Insensitive: He means well, but he can be a little inconsiderate. All Beavis wants is a ride to Maxi-Mart, but he keeps forcing him to go on errands with him and treats him like a buddy. It takes Beavis outright hollering at him that he needs to go hours later, for him to get it through his thick skull. Nice Guy: Compared to Butt-Head, Keith is a walk in the park, if a little inconsiderate.

characters.name: Shawna/Donna
characters.description: Old Beavis and Butt-Head's attractive next door neighbor, who they often try to hit on. All There in the Script: Her name is only seen in the credits of the episodes she appears in, and is yet to be addressed by it in the episodes themselves. (Although the Old duo call her "Donna" in "New Couch") Ascended Extra: Originally appeared as aOne-Shot Characterin Season 10's "Married", but got more appearances in Season 11. Catchphrase: "Creep!", whenever Old Beavis and Butt-Head try macking on her. Dope Slap: She tends to do this to the Old duo when they try to hit on her, especially to Old Butt-Head.

characters.name: Dr. Rod Johnson
characters.description: A doctor who runs Stork in a Bottle Sperm Bank, later known as Highland Fertility Clinic. Age Lift: Is significantly older in season 11 due to the time that passed while Beavis and Butt-Head were in the wormhole. The Bus Came Back: Subject to by far the longest gap between appearances, with a whooping 32 years between his initial appearance and his return in the 2022 revival (1993 and 2025). Unfortunate Names: One of at least a dozen characters whose name is a dick joke.

characters.name: Old Woman on Plane and Bus
characters.description: Accidental Misnaming: Calls the boys Travis and Bob-Head. Cool Old Lady: Is polite to the boys and is taking a bus trip across America after losing in Vegas. Distaff Counterpart: Can be considered this to Tom Anderson, as her advanced age and hearing loss causes her to view the boys as innocent and well mannered. Unlike Anderson, the boys, for the most part, treat her with respect. Nice Job Breaking It, Hero!: She unleashes Cornholio twice in the movie in an effort to help Beavis. The first time, she gives Beavis caffeine pills after he says he's tired. The second time, she tries to give Beavis Xanax after he gets beat up by the bus driver, but neither can read the label. No Name Given: Her name is never said in the movie itself. According to the screenplay, it's Martha.

characters.name: Dallas Grimes
characters.description: Aerith and Bob: With Muddy. Her name sounds much more conventionally usable than his. Big Bad Duumvirate: With her ex-husband Muddy. Muddy pushes the dimwitted duo into their adventure and provides an immediate threat while Dallas kickstarted the main conflict. Deadpan Snarker: When Agent Flemming threatens her with a cavity search, she smugly replies, "Is that a promise?" Fat and Skinny: The Skinny to Muddy's Fat. Knight of Cerebus: Dallas is an international criminal whose on the FBI's most wanted list and recently stole an incredibly potent bioweapon from the US government. Her role is played dead seriously as she very nearly killed the boys and only spared them because she figured they were too dimwitted and horny to disobey her orders.

characters.name: Muddy Grimes
characters.description: Aerith and Bob: With Dallas. It's hard to name a child "Muddy"for obvious reasons. The Alcoholic: He was drunk when meeting Beavis and Butthead, causing him to mistake the two for his hired hitmen. Big Bad Duumvirate: With his ex-wife Dallas. Muddy pushes the dimwitted duo into their adventure and provides an immediate threat while Dallas kickstarted the main conflict. Establishing Character Moment: He's first shown in a hotel room getting drunk and ordering a hit on his wife. When Beavis and Butthead shows up, he thinks they're the assassins. All of this establishes early on that he's the bad guy of the story. Fat and Skinny: The Fat to Dallas' Skinny.

characters.name: Agent Flemming
characters.description: All There in the Script: According to the script, his full name is Ryan Flemming. Black Comedy Rape: As aRunning Gag, he regularly orders cavity searches on people Beavis and Butt-Head encounter, including all the old people on the bus, the Andersons, Van Dreissen and even Butt-Head himself. The Comically Serious: His harsh nature and authoritative voice do little to make him seem imposing, as his obsessive habits reveal him to be a bit of an oddball.Robert Stackplays the part completely straight, no different than how he played Elliot Ness, regardless of the ridiculous things he encounters. Jerk with a Heart of Gold: He's far from the nicest guy and does a lot of questionable things but he does sincerely praise Beavis & Butthead at the end for stopping the virus and sets it up so they can meet and be thanked by President Clinton for their actions. Karma Houdini: He's not the villain of the story and is a lawful US agent whose extreme actions are for the purpose of protecting the country from a deadly biological weapon. However, he still commits multiple acts that go far beyond reasonable, freely handing out cavity searches to anyone who has even the loosest of connections to Beavis and Butt-head, throwing due process out the window and brutalizing people like Van Driessen, and basically punishing law-abiding citizens who are doing their duty by reporting to him that they saw Beavis and Butt-head. Despite that, Flemming never faces any sort of punishment for his actions andmighthave even gotten away with handing out cavity searches to Daria, Cassandra, and some Positive Acting Teens in the classroom (while he's not shown outright saying he's going to cavity search the class, it wouldn't be out-of-character for him to do so, considering how he does it to everyone else with reckless abandon).

characters.name: Agent Bork
characters.description: The Everyman: He's a pretty normal dude surrounded by insane people and insane situations. Only Sane Man: He's the only member of the ATF who acts relatively normal and reasonable. And even though he doesn't interfere with Flemming and the other agents going overboard with their cavity searches on account of the potential catastrophe the country was facing, he at least has the decency to not be overeager to engage in such extreme acts himself.

characters.name: Agent Hurly
characters.description: Black Comedy Rape: See the entry for this trope on Flemming. Hurly personally conducts all of Flemming's cavity searches. Butch Lesbian: Appears to be this stereotype but isAmbiguously Gayas it is never explicitly stated.

characters.name: Serena Ryan
characters.description: Ambiguous Situation: Did she really follow Smart Beavis and Smart Butt-Head because of Smart Beavis'Love Confession, or did she leave to avoid facing up to her mistakes? The fact that she took off after she and Smart Beavis scored and has ghosted him ever since suggests the latter. Contrasting Sequel Antagonist: Serena Ryan fills a very similar niche to Dallas Grimes from the first movie, particularly with the boys' desire to "score" with Serena driving the plot of the movie, much like with their attraction to Dallas but ends up being a very different kind of antagonist. Dress-wise, Dallas tends to wear more skimpy clothing while Serena dresses more modestly by comparison. While Dallas was an open criminal and terrorist, Serena managed to lead a more legit political career and whatever corrupt, criminal things she did were done in secrecy, without exposure. Dallas was also openly hostile to Beavis and Butt-head to begin with and despite acting seductive to get what she wanted out of them, had no intention of ever "scoring" with them and notably never undergoes aHeel–Face Turn. Serena, on the other hand, is actually genuinely friendly with the boys to begin with and despite growing more hostile to them throughout the movie, eventually gives up on that hostility, has herHeel Realization, and consents to their desires, albeit with some small reluctance. Corrupt Politician: Implies she did many underhanded methods to become governor. Hazy–Feel Turn: Towards the end of the movie, shesoftens her tone towards Beavis and Butt-head when she realizes they didn't want to kill her and stops being antagonistic towards them. On the other hand, she never outright expresses regret for the murders she committed in her political career and it's implied she slept with Smart Beavis to avoid answering for her crimes. After that, considering she doesn't appear again after the second movie, it's not too clear how much her personal moral compass has really changed. Heel Realization: Has on

characters.name: Jim Hartson
characters.description: Butt-Monkey:No one listens to him, and Serena treats him like a servant. This leads to him betraying her later on. Revenge Before Reason:He is so determined to expose Serena's crimes to get back at her mistreatment of him that he blocks off access to the portal the smart versions of the boys summoned with his body, and continues to stay in place while calling the Whistleblower's Hotline even while he's getting sucked in. What Happened to the Mouse?:What became of his fate after being sucked back into 1998 is never brought up again. And whether or not Hartson traveling back in time could drastically alter the timeline isn't considered either, since he apparently didn't die and could conceivably just try to target Serena back in the 90s.
